questions: Does flipping A_i mean toggling between two specific values (like 0/1) or does it mean changing A_i to its opposite (e.g., if A_i is 5, flipping makes it -5)?
Are A_i and B_i guaranteed to be integers, but are there constraints on their possible values (e.g., non-negative, binary)?
Can we perform multiple operations sequentially, and does the cost of each operation depend on the current state of A after previous operations?
Is the goal to make A identical to B after all operations, or must A match B immediately after each operation?
If flipping changes A_i to a different integer, what is the new value? For example, does flipping swap A_i with B_i or use a predefined set?
Are there any constraints on the order of operations or can we choose i arbitrarily each time?
Does the cost include the operation where no flip is performed (zero operations), and if so, is the cost for that operation zero?
Is the cost per operation always non-negative, and can the total cost be negative if some A_k are negative?
